title: Surgical and Diagnostic Procedure Terminology

sections.learningObjectives:
- Define common surgical and diagnostic procedure suffixes (-ectomy, -otomy, -ostomy, -plasty, -scopy, -centesis, -gram, -graphy, -metry).
- Distinguish among surgical procedure types by their suffix (removal, incision, opening, repair, fusion, suturing, crushing).
- Decode procedure and diagnostic test names from their word parts (roots, prefixes, and suffixes).
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of '-ectomy' as 'exit' — the part is taken out of the body, like removing a bad apple from a bowl.

### Question 2

An -otomy is like carefully cutting a small slit to get inside; the cut can then heal closed again.

### Question 3

-graphy is the act of taking the picture, while -gram is the picture itself.

### Question 4

-metry is like using a ruler — it tells you how much, how fast, or how big something is.

### Question 5

Append- means appendix, so an appendectomy is taking out the appendix.

### Question 6

Gastr- means stomach, so a gastrostomy makes a little door into the stomach.

### Question 7

A tracheotomy is a cut into the windpipe; a tracheostomy keeps a little opening there that stays open.

### Question 8

Arthr- means joint, so arthroscopy is using a tiny camera to look inside a joint.

### Question 9

Mammography is the special x-ray that takes pictures of the breast to look for problems.

### Question 10

Spirometry measures how much air you can blow in and out, like testing how strong a balloon is.

### Question 11

Hyster- means uterus, so a hysterectomy removes the uterus.

### Question 12

Mast- means breast, so a mastectomy removes breast tissue.

### Question 13

Cardi- means heart — think of 'cardio' exercise, which works your heart.

### Question 14

Nephr- means kidney. A doctor who studies kidneys is a nephrologist.

### Question 15

A colostomy makes a new exit for waste through the belly wall when part of the colon cannot work.

### Question 16

Arthrocentesis is like draining extra water from a swollen joint with a needle.

### Question 17

Laparoscopy uses a small camera through a tiny cut to look around the belly.

### Question 18

Rhin- means nose, so rhinoplasty is fixing or reshaping the nose.

### Question 19

Blephar- means eyelid, so blepharoplasty fixes the eyelid.

### Question 20

Cyst- here means bladder, so cystoscopy looks inside the bladder with a tiny camera.

### Question 21

An ECG draws the heart's electrical beats on paper, like a machine writing down your heartbeat.

### Question 22

-graphy is doing the recording; -gram is the paper it prints out.

### Question 23

Phlebotomy is making a tiny cut into a vein to collect blood for tests.

### Question 24

Myringotomy is a tiny cut in the eardrum, often to let fluid drain from the ear.

### Question 25

Osteotomy is cutting a bone, like sawing a board to reshape it.

### Question 26

Ostectomy removes a piece of bone; osteotomy just cuts it.

### Question 27

Nephr- means kidney, so a nephrectomy takes out a kidney.

### Question 28

Splen- means spleen, so a splenectomy removes the spleen.

### Question 29

Tonsillectomy takes out the tonsils at the back of the throat.

### Question 30

Oophor- means ovary, so an oophorectomy removes an ovary.

### Question 31

Salping- means fallopian tube, so a salpingectomy removes a fallopian tube.

### Question 32

Hysteroscopy is looking inside the uterus with a small camera.

### Question 33

Colposcopy looks closely at the cervix and vagina, like using a magnifying glass.

### Question 34

Endoscopy is using a small camera on a tube to look inside the body.

### Question 35

Bronchoscopy looks into the breathing tubes with a small camera.

### Question 36

Gastr- means stomach, so gastroscopy looks inside the stomach.

### Question 37

Laparotomy is a big cut to open the belly for surgery.

### Question 38

Craniotomy opens a small window in the skull to reach the brain.

### Question 39

Arthrodesis glues a joint together so it stops moving, which can stop pain.

### Question 40

Lithotripsy smashes a kidney stone into tiny pieces so they can pass out in urine.

### Question 41

Herniorrhaphy sews a bulge back into place, like stitching a hole in a pocket closed.

### Question 42

A biopsy takes a tiny piece of tissue so a doctor can look at it closely to check for disease.

### Question 43

The mammogram is the photo; mammography is the act of taking the photo.

### Question 44

A myelogram takes a special picture of the spinal cord to look for problems.

### Question 45

Echocardiography uses sound waves, like a bat's echolocation, to make moving pictures of the heart.

### Question 46

A spirometer is the machine you blow into; it measures how much air your lungs can move.

### Question 47

Cholecyst- means gallbladder, so a cholecystectomy removes the gallbladder.

### Question 48

A nephrostomy makes a little drain from the kidney to the outside so urine can escape.

### Question 49

Ureteroscopy looks inside the tube (ureter) that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

### Question 50

The angiogram is the picture of the blood vessels; angiography is taking that picture.

### Question 51

Venography takes pictures of the veins, the tubes that carry blood back to the heart.

### Question 52

Cyst- here means bladder, so a cystectomy removes the bladder.

### Question 53

Thyroidectomy removes part or all of the thyroid gland in the neck.

### Question 54

Cut = -otomy, take out = -ectomy, make a new opening = -ostomy. The order is cut, remove, open.

### Question 55

-gram is the finished picture; -graphy is taking it, -scopy is looking, and -metry is measuring.

### Question 56

Arthroscopy just looks; the other three fix or change the joint.

### Question 57

Anything ending in -centesis means a needle is used to draw fluid out.

### Question 58

To take out the uterus you need -ectomy; the other endings look, pin, or photograph it.

### Question 59

Oto- means ear, so otoscopy is looking into the ear.

### Question 60

Ophthalmoscopy looks inside the eye to check the retina and other parts.

### Question 61

This is taking out the gallbladder through small cuts using a camera instead of one big cut.

### Question 62

For breathing that lasts, you need a door that stays open (-ostomy), not just a cut (-otomy).

### Question 63

Total knee arthroplasty is giving the knee a new, smooth surface, like resurfacing a worn floor.

### Question 64

Phlebectomy takes a vein out; the others picture, cut, or fix it.

### Question 65

Aden- means gland, so an adenectomy removes a gland.

### Question 66

A myomectomy removes a noncancerous muscle lump, like taking a knot out of a rope.

### Question 67

Two word parts are joined: the tube and the ovary are both taken out.

### Question 68

Only the -ectomy word is surgery; the others take pictures or name a problem.

### Question 69

The assistant explains simply what the test is, then lets the doctor answer the harder safety questions.

### Question 70

The assistant helps set things up and explain; the doctor does the test, reads it, and decides it is needed.

### Question 71

The assistant puts the picture in the chart and makes sure the doctor sees it; the doctor explains the results.

### Question 72

Surgery words do things to the body; diagnostic words take pictures or measurements.
